correctness.rationale: Horváth's published k=2 formula is convex in y for fixed x, so the maximum lies at an endpoint of the admissible interval. The upper endpoint is x^2 with x^2<=1-1/n^2. The lower endpoint becomes a 2x2 Rayleigh quotient with largest eigenvalue lambda_n=1/2+(1/(2n))*sqrt(2(n^3-2n^2+2)/(n+1)). The positive top eigenvector is shown to satisfy the strict upper-facet inequality and is realized by an explicit supporting normal; all other facets violate the upper-facet condition. Thus 2n lambda_n is exactly the two-upper-facet maximum.

value.rationale: The primary source explicitly leaves the higher-dimensional reflected-simplex problem open. The two-upper-facet chamber is the first nontrivial chamber beyond the height-normal one-facet configuration and is exactly the chamber that realizes the known five-dimensional optimum. Its all-dimensional exact solution therefore supplies a natural structural benchmark, proves a uniform obstruction to the old 2n value from every n>=5 onward, and determines the asymptotic scale (1+sqrt(2))n.
